subject: maths

concepts.title: Multi-term Proportionality
concepts.definition: A relationship where multiple quantities maintain a constant ratio such that each term changes by the same scaling factor.
concepts.key_idea: All parts of a multi-term ratio scale by the same multiplier.
question_patterns: find the missing ingredient quantity given the ratio
calculate the amount of each part for a multi-term ratio
determine the required quantity of components for a specific total
how much of each item is needed to maintain the ratio
compute the missing values in a proportional multi-term sequence

solution_steps.explain: Divide the target quantity by the corresponding ratio part
Multiply the specific ratio term by the scaling factor

concepts.title: Dividing a Whole in Ratio
concepts.definition: The process of partitioning a total quantity into segments based on a defined ratio of parts.
concepts.key_idea: Total quantity is distributed based on the fractional weight of each ratio term.
question_patterns: divide the total into the given ratio
calculate the share of each component in the total
how many units of each part are needed for the total
distribute the quantity according to the specified ratio
find the individual portions of a whole based on the ratio

solution_steps.explain: Calculate the total number of parts
Multiply the total quantity by the fraction of the specific term

concepts.title: Inverse Proportions
concepts.definition: A relationship between two variables where an increase in one causes a proportional decrease in the other, keeping their product constant.
concepts.key_idea: The product of inversely proportional quantities remains invariant.
question_patterns: calculate the time taken if the number of workers changes
find the new duration given a change in speed
determine the quantity needed if the time factor is adjusted
how many days will the provisions last for a different number of people
compute the missing value in an inverse proportion table

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the known pair of values
Divide the constant product by the new value of the other variable
